points.description: Scope/accessibility of data members: a data member can be accessed (used) by any/all member functions of the class (shared across the class's member functions). Equivalent wording such as 'accessible throughout the class' is acceptable.

levels.says: Says data members are accessible within the class but vaguely (e.g. 'can be used in the class') without stating member functions can all access them.

points.description: Scope of local variables: a local variable can only be accessed/used inside the member function in which it is declared; other member functions cannot access it.

levels.says: Says local variables are only accessible 'inside a function' or 'in a block' without linking to the function that declares them (still correct but incomplete).

points.description: Where they are declared: data members are declared inside the class definition but outside any member function; local variables are declared inside the body of a member function.

Lifetime/persistence: data members belong to the object and persist for the object's lifetime (retaining values between function calls); local variables are created when the function is called and destroyed when it ends (values not retained). Accept any one correct contrast of this kind.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the scope contrast (data members: all member functions; local variables: only their own function), plus declaration location and lifetime. The model answer covers only scope, so scope alone earns up to 3 of 5; the extra two marks are for correct declaration-place and lifetime differences. No marks for reversed or incorrect statements.

selftest_notes: The model answer scored only 3 of 5.
